subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should OpenClaw expose ordinary third-party plugin-to-plugin Gateway method calls, and if so should that be raw method dispatch, an allowlisted request API, or a typed service/capability contract?
rationale: This changes the public Plugin SDK and Gateway authorization boundary, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API shape or security model.

options.title: Design a narrow authorized contract
options.body: Expose only approved plugin-owned methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep trusted-official only
options.body: Leave `api.runtime.gateway.request` limited to bundled or trusted official plugins and ask arbitrary third-party plugins to use existing HTTP or capability seams.

options.title: Allow raw Gateway dispatch
options.body: Expose a generic method-string caller and accept the larger security, compatibility, and schema-stability surface as an explicit product decision.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authorized contract
recommendation.body: Expose only approved plugin-owned methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the current partial trusted-plugin surface and authored the earlier route-scoped dispatch contract, making him the strongest decision owner from history.
